Found **one merge-blocking bug** in `share-editing`:

**[P1] View-only shares can edit unlocked documents — `src/guard.js:12`**
`share.mask & WRITE === WRITE` is parsed as `share.mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`. Since that comparison is always `true`, it effectively checks bit 1 (`READ`), not bit 4 (`WRITE`).

Confirmed:
- Viewer (`mask: 1`): `canEdit` returns **true**.
- Commenter without WRITE (`mask: 3`): returns **true**.
- WRITE-only share (`mask: 4`): returns **0** (denied).

Use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE) && !share.locked`, consistent with `canComment`. Add tests denying edits for viewers and commenters; the existing editor test masks the bug because editors have both READ and WRITE.

All **6 existing tests pass**. I also checked toggle behavior across all 16 masks and ownership transfers between distinct users; no additional issues found there.

**No code changed. I’d fix the permission check before merging.**
